3. Defendants-petitioners field Civil Revision case No. 153 of 1984 before this Court against the judgment dated 6.3.84. After the disposal of the Civil Revision Case No. 153 of 1984, defendants-petitioners discovered certain number for new things and important matters and evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence, were not within their knowledge at any time prioer to the disposal of the said Revision Case and there were errors of law apparent on the face of the record. In Civil Revision Case No. 153 of 1984, this court observed that the learned Advocate for the petitioner did not press ground of limitation as set out in the application probably realising that the suit is well within time and this observation was made with due consideration of section 3 of the Limitation Act which provides that the suit filed after expiry of limitation will be dismissed even if ground of limitation has not been pressed by defendants. Plaintiff opposite parties were admittedly out of possession from 2.2.66 and the suit not filed within six years from this date and the suit was barred by limitation. 

 4. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners has pressed the ground of Limitation and in this connection the learned Advocate for the petitioners referred to article XLVII of the Limitation Act and urged that period of Limitation begins to run from the date of the final order in the case. In this connection the learned Advocate urged that where order is passed by Magistrate under section 245(C) of Criminal Procedure Code, that order is to be treated as final order and Limitation starts running from the date of that order. It appears that the petitioners of the review petition figured as 2nd party in 145 who passed final order on 8.1.66. The suit was filed on 21.5.69 and as such suit being hit by Limitation does not arise as it was filed within period of Limitation. The Title Suit was initially numbered as T.S. No. 88 at 1981. The suit was initially filed on 29.4.68 and the final order in 145 proceedings was passed on 8.1.66. Therefore, on calculation it is found that the suit is well within time and for that reason this Court observed that Mr. P.K. Bosu, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, abandoned the ground of Limitation taken in the application and urged that the suit land is beet land and as such it is to be treated as fishery and by operation of law it vested in Government. The learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners thus consciously did not press the ground of limitation. 

 Further, it appears that suit was filed within three years from the final order passed in 145 Cr. P.C. proceedings by the learned Munsif Magistrate So, this ground of limitation has no substance at all.
